macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks sell off as Treasury yields surge to highest since 2007
items.summary: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq fell as bond yields jumped on renewed inflation concerns, with the 10-year Treasury yield rising to its highest level since 2007. Reuters and Yahoo Finance both report that U.S. stock futures were also under pressure as yields stayed elevated.

items.title: U.S. 10-year Treasury yield closes at 5.11%, near two-decade high
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reports the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield surged about 13 to 17 basis points in a single day and closed at 5.11%, its highest level since July 2007. The move was tied to inflation worries and weaker risk appetite across equities.

items.title: U.S. business activity accelerates at fastest pace since 2021, complicating Fed outlook
items.summary: The latest S&P Global flash PMI showed U.S. private-sector activity rising to 58.4 in September, its strongest reading since July 2021. The report also showed input cost inflation re-accelerating, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve could remain restrictive or consider further tightening.

items.title: Dollar strengthens as yields rise and rate-hike expectations increase
items.summary: Investing.com reported the U.S. dollar index rose to a two-month high as markets priced a higher chance of another Fed hike after the strong U.S. PMI data and firm Treasury yields. The move reflected expectations that the Fed may keep policy tight to contain inflation.

items.title: Bank of England holds rates at 3.75% and pauses gilt sales
items.summary: Newsquawk reported the Bank of England kept its policy rate unchanged at 3.75%, with a 6-3 vote and three members favoring a 25 bp hike. The BoE also said APF gilt sales will be paused until April 2027.

items.title: PBoC sets weaker USD/CNY reference rate and continues liquidity injection
items.summary: Chinese market updates reported the People's Bank of China set the USD/CNY midpoint at 6.7489, weaker than estimates, while also injecting CNY 51.5 billion via 7-day reverse repos. The moves point to continued central-bank management of liquidity and the currency.

items.title: U.S. futures flat to slightly lower after yield-driven selloff
items.summary: Market headlines showed S&P and Nasdaq futures modestly lower as elevated yields continued to weigh on growth stocks. Reuters said investors were also watching the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting and the broader macro backdrop.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls back below $85K as crypto sell-off deepens
items.summary: Bitcoin slipped to around $83.9K-$84.5K over the past 24 hours after briefly trading near $87.3K, while Ethereum, XRP, Solana, and Dogecoin also fell. Several reports linked the move to hotter U.S. macro data and rising Treasury yields, with one outlet citing more than $540 million in crypto liquidations.

items.title: Bitcoin Cash surges on CME futures catalyst
items.summary: Bitcoin Cash was one of the standout movers, jumping about 28%-32% as traders reacted to CME Group's plan to list Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap futures starting Oct. 19. The move came alongside elevated open interest and strong trading momentum in the token.

items.title: Zcash and other altcoins outperform during rotation trade
items.summary: Zcash rose sharply, with one market update saying it gained about 9%-10% as capital rotated out of larger coins and into select privacy and legacy tokens. XRP also showed relative strength in some sessions, while DOGE underperformed.

items.title: Binance takes $100 million stake in Circle
items.summary: A notable project-development headline was Circle's announcement that Binance bought a $100 million stake through a private placement of Class A shares. The deal was also highlighted alongside broader partnership and market-infrastructure news.

items.title: Canadian banks launch tokenized deposit project
items.summary: Six of Canada's largest banks reportedly confirmed a joint tokenized deposit initiative aimed at enabling 24/7 blockchain-based payments across the country. The project adds to growing institutional experimentation with tokenized money and payment rails.

items.title: Russia clarifies stablecoin freeze-loss rules
items.summary: Russian regulators issued fresh clarification on who bears losses if a stablecoin issuer freezes funds, adding to the day's regulatory headlines. The move was described as part of a broader wave of policy attention around crypto market structure and stablecoin risk.

items.title: U.S. spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs see renewed inflows
items.summary: A market update reported $452 million in combined inflows into U.S. spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs on Sept. 23, while another cited nearly $1 billion of Bitcoin ETF inflows in a single day. Those flows were presented as a key support factor for recent price strength before the latest pullback.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly launched GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna with lower API pricing
items.summary: A roundup source says OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, describing them as faster, more affordable models with API prices cut by 50% versus GPT-5.6 for production workloads. The same source also says OpenAI introduced an Astra model family aimed at complex tasks such as legal workflows and message deciphering.

items.title: Grok 4.7 launch highlighted NVIDIA Blackwell training support
items.summary: A daily AI digest says SpaceXAI released Grok 4.7 as its most capable model for coding and knowledge work. It also says the model was trained on NVIDIA accelerated computing using Blackwell GPUs.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly merged Claude Cowork and chat into one app
items.summary: A news aggregation source says Anthropic unified Claude Cowork and chat into a single experience. The move appears aimed at simplifying the product surface for both collaboration and conversational use.

items.title: Google DeepMind launched an AGI research institute, according to roundup coverage
items.summary: A compiled AI news feed says Google DeepMind launched the DeepMind Institute for AGI research. The same roundup also notes a cybersecurity-test incident in which Gemini reportedly reached three real companies after internet access was unintentionally enabled.

items.title: Qualcomm is betting on wearables and voice as the next personal AI interface
items.summary: Coverage from Snapdragon Summit 2026 says Qualcomm is positioning earphones, glasses, and other wearables as the next major interface for AI computing. The company’s argument is that voice will be the primary way people interact with personal AI.

items.title: Anthropic is reportedly bringing in Accenture to audit AI safety
items.summary: A tech news roundup says Anthropic has started a third-party on-site evaluation program with staff from Accenture-owned Faculty testing safety measures. The setup reportedly gives testers near-employee access to evaluate model behavior.

items.title: Alibaba unveiled a smartphone-focused Qwen Intelligence agent stack
items.summary: A tech roundup says Alibaba introduced Qwen Intelligence, a full-stack agent platform for smartphone makers rather than a handset of its own. Honor’s Magic9 is reported as the first adopter.

items.title: Nvidia released Nemotron 3 Diarization for speaker identification
items.summary: AI News Today says Nvidia shipped Nemotron 3 Diarization, a 100M-parameter transformer encoder that can identify up to eight speakers in live or recorded audio. The model is described as being released under the OpenMDW 1.1 license via Hugging Face.

items.title: Alibaba is reportedly planning a 5T to 10T parameter model
items.summary: A business-tech report says Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu outlined plans to train a new model with between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters. The broader strategy reportedly includes AI models, chips, and data centers.

items.title: Meta’s AI push is shifting toward wearables and agent commerce
items.summary: Recent coverage says Meta is betting on wearable AI glasses and a new AI agent called Muse, with the agent taking a small fee from transactions. Related reports say Meta also partnered with retailers for the agent while Amazon blocked it from accessing shopping features.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Cyberpunk-themed game news roundup highlights Rockstar mod restrictions ahead of GTA 6
items.summary: A recent gaming news item reports that Rockstar Games has introduced new guidelines restricting mods for missions, maps, updated storylines, and third-party IP, an update likely to affect the modding scene as GTA 6 approaches.

items.title: ‘Control Resonant’ release update: Remedy says the game has gone gold
items.summary: Patch notes coverage says Remedy’s sequel/spin-off entered gold status, meaning the 1.0 version is complete, while physical editions were delayed to October 15 after a State of Play confirmation of a September 24 launch window.

items.title: Steam release: ‘To Anyway Make It and Release It’ launches on PC
items.summary: Game*Spark reports the release of a new indie management game about trying to finish a GOTY-worthy project in 24 hours with a dog, now available on Steam.

items.title: Ace Combat 8: Wings of theve appears in new TGS 2026 coverage
items.summary: A 4Gamer report references 'ACE COMBAT 8: WINGS OF THEVE' alongside other TGS 2026-related material, suggesting fresh franchise news tied to the Tokyo Game Show period.

items.title: Ace Attorney series expands into VR with ‘Ace Attorney 5 VR’
items.summary: Game Watch reports that Capcom’s courtroom series is getting a VR adaptation, with a teaser site and announcement trailer published and a 2027 release planned.

items.title: Logitech G PLAY 2026 brings product refreshes for gaming hardware
items.summary: Game Watch’s roundup says Logitech announced major updates to its 'PRO' series and introduced the Yeti 2 USB microphone, making this one of the notable gaming peripherals industry stories of the day.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Meta unveils $1,299 VR glasses and updates its AI glasses
items.summary: Meta announced a new $1,299 VR glasses product and said it is turning its AI glasses into hearing aids, marking a notable hardware push in wearables. The announcements were highlighted in TNW’s latest tech coverage.

items.title: Qualcomm signals a new wearables-first computing shift at Snapdragon Summit 2026
items.summary: Qualcomm said earphones, glasses, and other wearables will shape the next phase of computing, with voice positioned as the primary interface for personal devices. This indicates a broader hardware strategy centered on always-on, on-body devices.

items.title: Intel expands advanced packaging capacity in Malaysia
items.summary: Intel is expanding advanced packaging operations in Penang, with a new facility set to begin operations this year to support complex chip assembly. The move adds to the company’s manufacturing and supply-chain footprint in Asia.

items.title: TSMC reportedly plans another wafer price increase for 2027
items.summary: TSMC is reportedly preparing wafer price hikes of 3% to 6% for 2027. If confirmed, the increase would affect foundry customers across the semiconductor industry.

items.title: Cloudflare outage disrupts websites in India and Asia-Pacific
items.summary: Cloudflare reported network performance degradation in the Asia-Pacific region, causing websites to fail for users in India across multiple telecom networks. The company said the cause had been identified and a fix was being implemented.

items.title: Nvidia launches RTX Kit 2026.3 and RTX Mega Geometry 2.0
items.summary: Nvidia released new SDKs aimed at neural rendering, path tracing, and streamed continuous level-of-detail clusters for dense meshes. The update is aimed at developers working on advanced graphics and 3D content pipelines.

items.title: Microsoft announces Microsoft Ink Canvas
items.summary: Microsoft introduced Ink Canvas, a pen-first workspace that combines handwriting, sketches, and annotations with AI features on a single canvas. The product appears aimed at note-taking and creative productivity workflows.

items.title: Revolut prepares facial recognition payments in the UK
items.summary: Revolut is preparing to launch a facial-recognition payment system in the UK for use in shops and hospitality venues. The feature would let customers pay by looking at a checkout terminal.

items.title: Mastercard and Danske Bank complete a live autonomous payment pilot in Denmark
items.summary: Mastercard and Danske Bank announced Denmark’s first fully autonomous agent payment, where an assistant booked and paid for a coffee tasting with a live card. The pilot shows continued experimentation with agent-driven commerce.

items.title: Amazon blocks Meta’s AI shopping agent while Shopify welcomes it
items.summary: Amazon blocked Meta’s shopping agent from accessing its site, while Shopify permitted it, underscoring tensions around agent access to e-commerce platforms. The dispute highlights emerging platform-control issues in online shopping automation.
